answer: To mint influence, an agent posts collateral and proves exclusive control of one scarce off-chain handle—a paid domain or a UTXO locked to a single pubkey. The proof is a challenge-response posted at a public jetty. Independent verifiers act as a prism: each re-queries the handle and accepts it only if it is still uniquely bound. Checks repeat at dawn every epoch. A reused handle or a late proof burns every linked deposit. An attacker who wants a hundred voters must buy a hundred separate handles and keep a hundred deposits at risk; cheap extra keypairs add no weight.
